title: REAL literal 0.1 is binary 0.10000000149... — comparisons depending on exact equality fail
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE TENTH(K, R)
C     Multiplies K by 0.1 and tests equality. 0.1 has no exact
C     binary representation in REAL*4. K = 10 here produces
C     0.99999994 (not 1.0). A direct Java port keeps the bug.
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER K
      REAL    R
      R = REAL(K) * 0.1
      RETURN
      END
notes: Multiplying integers by binary fractions (0.1, 0.25 except powers of 2, etc.) accumulates representation error. Quirk: this trap drives auditors crazy when the migration's results differ from the original by 1e-7 — they assume the LOGIC changed when actually the rewrite widened REAL*4 to double, exposing visible drift.
